title: Sum of Squares Rank of Biquadratic Forms and The Zarankiewicz Number
summary: Denote the maximum sos rank of $m \times n$ sum of squares (SOS) biquadratic forms by $BSR(m, n)$. In this paper, we show that $BSR(m, n) \ge z(m, n)$ and conjecture that $BSR(m, n) = z(m, n)$, where $z(m, n)$ is the Zarankiewicz number. Our result coincides with the existing results for $m = 2$, $n = 2$, and $m = n = 3$, and is superior to other previously known lower bounds. Our result also connects graph theory and SOS polynomial theory.
